rv.q: “Safe House,” which would seem in form and subject matter a natural successor, is far neater, but so verbally pared back that it gives the audience too little to hold onto.
Attending Safe House is an immersive, hypnotic experience filled with haunting song, spell-binding spectacle, and an undercurrent of feeling.

The combination of Mullarkey’s wistful music, Gilmore’s achingly vulnerable performance, and Walsh’s command of the production elements builds a striking environment and creates a mood, but little beyond mood.
Theater 'Safe House' updates the memory play as a musical scrapbook (Off Broadway review) Date: February 20, 2025. Author: Thom Geier How do we cope with the trauma of our past?

cn.t: Enda Walsh's one-woman show about Irish childhood memories captures melancholy effectively but offers little else, leaving critics divided on its sparse, multimedia storytelling at St. Ann's Warehouse.

vr.q: I think if you're open to something that requires that level of engagement or you like experimental pieces that demand dissection and interpretation, this is for you.
